summary: The prepared_gaia implementation uses the SPADE XMPP-based multi-agent framework with five well-named agents and ontology-labelled message exchanges, representing the most structurally complete of the three versions. However, it cannot run as written: `asyncio` is not imported in road_condition_reporter.py causing a NameError, all PeriodicBehaviour subclasses are instantiated without the required `period` argument, and the NavigationManagerAgent never sends `change-light` commands despite receiving traffic-light state, leaving the traffic-light adaptation loop unimplemented. Route waypoints are hardcoded regardless of conditions.

findings.description: road_condition_reporter.py uses `await asyncio.sleep(5)` inside SendRoadConditionBehaviour.run() but never imports asyncio. This raises NameError: name 'asyncio' is not defined at runtime, immediately crashing the RoadConditionReporterAgent and halting event monitoring.
findings.evidence: road_condition_reporter.py line 40: `await asyncio.sleep(5)` — asyncio is absent from the import block at lines 1–6.

findings.description: All three PeriodicBehaviour subclasses (VehicleNavigatorAgent.SendPositionBehaviour, TrafficLightControllerAgent.SendTrafficLightStateBehaviour, RoadConditionReporterAgent.SendRoadConditionBehaviour) are added with no `period` argument. SPADE's PeriodicBehaviour.__init__ requires a period parameter; omitting it will cause instantiation failure or undefined scheduling behaviour.
findings.evidence: vehicle_navigator.py line 21: `self.add_behaviour(self.SendPositionBehaviour())` — no period; traffic_light_controller.py line 19: `self.add_behaviour(self.SendTrafficLightStateBehaviour())` — no period; road_condition_reporter.py line 24: `self.add_behaviour(self.SendRoadConditionBehaviour())` — no period.

findings.description: NavigationManagerAgent receives traffic light state from TrafficLightControllerAgent via the 'traffic-light-state' ontology and stores it in self.traffic_light_states, but never sends a 'change-light' message back to the controller. The control loop is open: traffic lights cannot be adapted to the vehicle's route.
findings.evidence: navigation_manager.py lines 54–63: AwaitTrafficLightStateBehaviour stores state only; no behaviour or method in NavigationManagerAgent sends a message with ontology 'change-light' to traffic_light@localhost.

findings.description: NavigationManagerAgent.generate_route() always returns the hardcoded waypoint list ['A','C','D','B'] regardless of vehicle positions, road conditions, or traffic light states collected in self.road_conditions and self.vehicle_positions. Conditions are included in the response body but do not influence the actual path.
findings.evidence: navigation_manager.py lines 99–108: `'waypoints': ['A', 'C', 'D', 'B']` is a literal; road_conditions appears only in `'conditions': self.road_conditions` as metadata, not as routing input.

findings.description: VehicleNavigatorAgent sends its own position periodically to NavigationManagerAgent, satisfying position tracking for the emergency vehicle. However, regular (non-privileged) vehicle positions are never reported or tracked; the requirement to read positions of both the privileged and ordinary vehicles is only half met.
findings.evidence: vehicle_navigator.py lines 23–38: SendPositionBehaviour sends only self.agent.current_position; no other VehicleNavigatorAgent instances or ordinary vehicle agents are created in main.py.

findings.description: DriverAlertingSystemAgent generates console-printed alerts about the approaching vehicle's route, satisfying the requirement conceptually. However, alerts are only stored in a local list and printed to stdout; no actual push notification to an application or external display is implemented.
findings.evidence: driver_alerting_system.py lines 39–45: alert dict appended to self.agent.alerts and printed with print(); no HTTP call, push notification, or display protocol is present.

findings.description: Both VehicleNavigatorAgent.RequestRouteBehaviour and DriverAlertingSystemAgent.RequestRouteBehaviour send route-request messages to NavigationManagerAgent using identical ontology ('route-request'). NavigationManagerAgent's single AwaitRouteRequestBehaviour cannot distinguish the requester's role, potentially responding to the wrong agent or causing message contention.
findings.evidence: vehicle_navigator.py line 44 and driver_alerting_system.py line 26: both send `metadata={'performative': 'request', 'ontology': 'route-request'}` to navigation_manager@localhost.

findings.description: SPADE agents require a running XMPP server at localhost for inter-agent communication. This prerequisite is not mentioned in README.md; users following the documented `python main.py` command will get connection errors with no guidance.
findings.evidence: README.md lines 31–33: only `python main.py` is documented; main.py lines 21–25: all agents are created with `@localhost` JIDs requiring an XMPP server.

findings.description: The use of SPADE with ontology-labelled messages (vehicle-position, route-request, route-response, road-condition, traffic-light-state, change-light) provides a structured, extensible communication protocol. Agent responsibilities are clearly named and separated across individual files, making the architecture easy to navigate.
findings.evidence: vehicle_navigator.py, traffic_light_controller.py, road_condition_reporter.py, driver_alerting_system.py, navigation_manager.py: each file contains exactly one agent class; ontology strings are consistent across sender and receiver templates.

findings.description: The included simple_simulation.py provides a working standalone simulation of the same logic without requiring SPADE or an XMPP server, demonstrating the intended data flow and serving as a useful fallback for development and testing.
findings.evidence: simple_simulation.py lines 1–186: full simulation loop exercising NavigationManager, VehicleNavigator, TrafficLightController, RoadConditionReporter, and DriverAlertingSystem without external dependencies.

missing_requirements: Sygnalizacja świetlna jest monitorowana i dostosowuje się do trasy pojazdu — NavigationManagerAgent never sends change-light commands; traffic lights cannot be adapted to the vehicle route.
Pozycja zwykłych pojazdów jest na bieżąco odczytywana — only the single emergency vehicle's position is tracked; ordinary vehicle positions are not monitored.
logical_inconsistencies: NavigationManagerAgent collects traffic_light_states from TrafficLightControllerAgent but never uses this data to issue change-light commands, breaking the intended monitoring-and-adaptation control loop.

Both VehicleNavigatorAgent and DriverAlertingSystemAgent send identical route-request messages to NavigationManagerAgent with the same ontology, making it impossible for NavigationManagerAgent to distinguish their roles or respond differently.

NavigationManagerAgent.GenerateRouteBehaviour waits 10 seconds then checks `if self.agent.vehicle_positions and self.agent.road_conditions` before generating a route, but NavigationManagerAgent also generates a route immediately on demand in AwaitRouteRequestBehaviour.run() via get_route(), making the periodic generation redundant.

RoadConditionReporterAgent.SendRoadConditionBehaviour attempts `await asyncio.sleep(5)` inside a PeriodicBehaviour, which is semantically wrong (PeriodicBehaviour already handles scheduling) and causes a NameError because asyncio is not imported.
implementation_risks: System cannot start due to the missing asyncio import in road_condition_reporter.py — road condition monitoring is entirely non-functional.
PeriodicBehaviour instantiation without a period argument will fail or produce undefined scheduling behaviour in the SPADE runtime, disabling position broadcasting and traffic-light state reporting.
Running the system requires an undocumented local XMPP server; without it, all agents will fail to connect and no inter-agent communication will occur.
Hardcoded A→C→D→B route in NavigationManagerAgent means route adaptation to real-time conditions is structurally impossible without a fundamental rewrite of generate_route().
